title: useState: a value and a setter

slides.say: Use state gives your component a memory. Here is how it works.
Call use state with the starting value. It returns exactly two things: the current value, index, and a setter, set index.

slides.text: The setter updates the value AND tells React to render again.
slides.say: Calling the setter does both jobs. React keeps the new value, and it renders the component again.

slides.text: Name them [something, setSomething]. Call useState at the top level only.
slides.say: Name the pair something and set something. And like every Hook, call it at the top level, never in loops or conditions.
